rationale: It bolts the two best archived operating legs together *and* silently swaps the trap term from NEG(MIN(...)) to NEG(MUL(...)), so any result is uninterpretable relative to both PersistentReleaseVerifiedValue and TrapFreeVerifiedValue, and the nested SUMRANK stacking is a kitchen-sink combination rather than a new mechanism.

A clean single-operator change to TrapFreeVerifiedValue (MIN→product of red-flag percentiles) with a coherent argument that MIN discards the magnitude of the larger flag, though the economic content is only modestly different and it remains a functional-form tweak of an already-tested signal rather than a new mechanism.

Coarsening the financing leg to a buyback-persistence count is a defensible and untested extension of the archive's persistence result, but the resulting signal has only ~16 distinct quality values so the value gate will do most of the sorting and any gain may reflect reduced turnover rather than new information.

The within-year co-occurrence count is a genuinely distinct hypothesis that no archived rank-sum can resolve, the construction matches the stated mechanism, and it is parsimonious — the main risk is coarseness and a possibly sparse high-score group.

This is a one-operator ablation of EqualWeightSelfFundedValue whose content is already spanned by SelfFundedGrowthValue (same three legs, nested weighting), and the only economic difference — industry centering flipping the gate's sign for below-average quality — is a known architectural feature rather than a new hypothesis.

The strict triple conjunction is a substantively different short-side construction from StaleWorkingCapitalTrap and gives useful sign-symmetric evidence, but the product of four percentiles is heavily mass-concentrated near zero and the multiplicative value gate implies expensive, flag-laden firms are assigned the high-return end, which is economically incoherent.
